title: Agent passport
description: An agent's versioned metadata: who it is, who owns it, what it may and may not do, and which versions of its model, prompt and policy it runs. It points at the agent's execution contract and approval policy and can only narrow them. Design: docs/assurance-loop.md.

passport.description: The persona's name, the same as its card's and its skill's or agent's directory.

version.description: Bumped on any change to the passport, including a change to any pin.

owner.description: The GitHub account or team accountable for the agent: @account or @org/team.

contract.description: The execution contract the agent runs under (contracts/<capability>/contract.json).

policy.description: The approval policy the agent is held to, as a path from the repo root, and its version.

permissions.description: What the agent may do, narrowed from its contract. Every action granted or under approval is one the contract grants or puts under approval, and nothing the contract puts under approval is granted. Anything in no list is denied.

never.description: Actions the agent may not take even with a human's approval. Each becomes a prohibition when the engine decides the agent's steps.

budget.description: Ceilings for one invocation, each at most the contract's. A figure the passport leaves out is the contract's.

delegates.description: The passports this agent may delegate to.

pins.description: The versions the agent runs on. A change to any of them is a new passport version.

model.description: The model by its catalog publisher, name and version. Left out for an agent run inside a harness, which picks the model.

prompt.description: Every file the agent's prompt is built from, as a path from the repo root, with its SHA-256 (CRLF line endings read as LF).

policy.description: The SHA-256 of the approval policy file named in policy.ruleset (CRLF line endings read as LF).

eval.description: The agent's trust evaluation. Needs a model pin, since a baseline belongs to a model.

suite.description: The cases file, as a path from the repo root. A case marked critical is one where the wrong answer lets a consequential action through.

baseline.description: The cases a run met, and the results.jsonl entry that records the run. deploy.sh promotes the passport only when that run was made against its exact pins.

result.description: The results.jsonl file, as a path from the repo root, and the entry's id: path#id.

threshold.description: How many cases below the baseline a run may meet before it drifts. A missed critical case is drift whatever the threshold.
